messages:
maria_support: FYI customer ACME (acct-acme-prod) reporting recurring p95 regressions during steady traffic window. p95 was ~180ms last week, now seeing 800ms-1.2s spikes. Ticket: https://support.redwood.ai/t/ACME-512. Need a repro pack: request ids, curl reproductions, token counts, promptset, and a short load plan we can run locally.

tyler_sre: can you grab a few request ids for the affected window? ideally ~10 that show high p95 and a couple normal ones for baseline. also include which model + max_tokens used.

maria_support: grabbing now, will pull from logs for 2026-03-15 10:00-10:30 UTC. sample ids I already saw: rq_38291a, rq_382b2f, rq_3830f1. model was redwood-2-large, max_tokens: 512, typical prompt length ~120 tokens.

alex_kg: thanks. when you post the request ids, include the full request headers if possible (authorization redacted) so eng can reproduce with the same routing headers (x-region/x-customer-tier). also add any client-side concurrency (client reported 40 concurrent streams).

ingrid_repro: I'll assemble a quick vegeta plan and a curl pack. For initial repro we should do: 50 concurrent connections, sustained 3m at 120 rps, payloads with token lengths: short (80), medium (300), long (900). That should surface batching/KV-cache behavior.

ingrid_repro: vegeta attack template:
```
# vegeta attack for chat-completions (replace API_KEY + ENDPOINT)
echo '{"model":"redwood-2-large","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":512}' > payload.json
cat payload.json | vegeta attack -duration=3m -rate=120 -connections=50 -header='Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY' -header='Content-Type: application/json' | vegeta report
```

maria_support: posting a curated list of 12 request ids with labels (high/normal) + curl reproductions for two examples:
- rq_38291a HIGH 2026-03-15T10:03:11Z
- rq_382b2f HIGH 2026-03-15T10:05:27Z
- rq_3830f1 NORMAL 2026-03-15T10:07:02Z
- rq_3835aa HIGH 2026-03-15T10:12:44Z
- rq_384ff0 HIGH 2026-03-15T10:20:09Z
- rq_384fff NORMAL 2026-03-15T10:22:11Z
(plus 6 more in the debug bundle)

maria_support: example curl (redacted tokens):
```
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Region: us-west-2" \
  -H "X-Customer-Tier: dedicated" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-large","input":"<...>","max_tokens":512}'
```

tyler_sre: perfect. please also collect the request trace logs from the serving nodes for those ids: /var/log/redwood/serving/*.log around the timestamps. the KV cache hit rates and batch sizes would help. if you can run the internal request-id extractor, that helps: `scripts/extract-req-logs --ids rq_38291a,rq_382b2f --out acme-reqs.log`

maria_support: done, uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-debug/acme/2005001234/req-logs.tar.gz

ingrid_repro: next step: generate a debug-bundle so we can share with runtime team. Use the debug-bot: `/debug-bundle create --ids rq_38291a,rq_382b2f,rq_3830f1 --note "ACME p95 regression 10:00-10:30"`

deploybot: debug-bundle created by maria_support: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/DBG-2005001234.tar.gz :package: (contains request traces, runtime profiles, kernel selection summaries)

tyler_sre: grabbing the bundle now. initial quick checks: I see variable batch sizes (1-40) and occasional kernel fallback to FP16 path at ~10:03:11 which correlates with rq_38291a. could be resource contention on gpu nodes.

alyx_check: (private note) also look at autoscaler logs for that period — any unexpected scale-downs?

maria_support: customer notes they had a client-side spike of 300 concurrent user sessions for a 90s burst starting 10:04. they claim backend should handle that, but we need to reproduce. I have the client-side HAR and a short script they used.

ingrid_repro: propose two repro plans:
- Plan A (light): 120 RPS sustained, concurrency 50, 3m, mixed promptset (80/300/900 tokens)
- Plan B (burst): start at 30 RPS, ramp to 300 RPS over 30s, hold 90s, then drop; concurrency 200 (simulates client burst).

ingrid_repro: also include a small curl pack for single-shot reproduction (use the exact headers):
```
# single-shot reproducer for rq_38291a
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'X-Request-ID: rq_38291a' \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2-large","input":"<PROMPT>","max_tokens":512,"stream":false}'
```

tyler_sre: thumbs up. once you run the vegeta Plan B please attach the generated HAR/vegeta results and the top 10 slow request ids. we want to see if the same request ids (or similar) spike consistently. :thumbsup:

maria_support: running Plan B in a sandbox now (using customer promptset). will share vegeta output and HAR. ETA 25m.

ingrid_repro: checklist for the debug pack upload to the ticket: request ids, curl pack, vegeta plan file, promptset (12 prompts), token counts table (prompt tokens / max_tokens), node-level metrics snapshot (CPU/GPU mem, kernel paths), autoscaler events, and debug-bundle link.

tyler_sre: if Plan B reproduces, we should try reproducing with `batching.disabled=true` or reduced batch size to isolate batching vs kernel-level problem. add that as variant run.

maria_support: upload after Plan B run: s3://redwood-debug/acme/2005001234/vegeta-planB-results.tar.gz

deploybot: upload complete: https://internal.redwood/snapshots/VEG-2005001234/results.tar.gz

ingrid_repro: quick summary from runs: Plan A p95 ~210ms (baseline), Plan B p95 median ~980ms with 5% of requests hitting >1.1s. top slow requests: rq_38291a, rq_3835aa, rq_384ff0. I attached vegeta output and top request traces in the bundle.

maria_support: added summary to ticket and notified customer. waiting on eng investigation for kernel fallback and autoscaler events. thanks all. :eyes:
